SuperAdmin.title: SuperAdmin
SuperAdmin.description: Represents the platform owner with full control over the system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Super Admin entity.

email.description: Email address of the Super Admin.

firstName.description: First name of the Super Admin.

lastName.description: Last name of the Super Admin.

Vendor.title: Vendor
Vendor.description: Represents a business using the platform to manage their parking lot.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Vendor entity.

spotLimit.description: The maximum number of parking spots the vendor can manage.

EndUser.title: EndUser
EndUser.description: Represents an end user who reserves and pays for parking spots.

id.description: Unique identifier for the EndUser entity.

email.description: Email address of the end user.

firstName.description: First name of the end user.

lastName.description: Last name of the end user.

vehiclePhotoUrl.description: URL of the users vehicle photo.

licensePlatePhotoUrl.description: URL of the users license plate photo.

ParkingSpot.title: ParkingSpot
ParkingSpot.description: Represents an individual parking spot within a vendor's parking lot.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ParkingSpot entity.

name.description: Name or identifier of the parking spot (e.g., 'A1', 'Spot 1').

isAvailable.description: Indicates whether the parking spot is currently available.

Invoice.title: Invoice
Invoice.description: Represents an invoice for a vendor's subscription or an end user's parking fees.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Invoice entity.

vendorId.description: Reference to Vendor. (Relationship: Vendor 1:N Invoice). Nullable if invoice is for end user

endUserId.description: Reference to EndUser. (Relationship: EndUser 1:N Invoice). Nullable if invoice is for vendor

amount.description: The total amount due on the invoice.

pdfUrl.description: URL of the invoice PDF file.

Conversation.title: Conversation
Conversation.description: Represents a conversation thread between a Super Admin and a Vendor Admin, or a Vendor Admin and an End User.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Conversation entity.

superAdminId.description: Reference to SuperAdmin. (Relationship: SuperAdmin 1:N Conversation). Nullable if conversation is between Vendor Admin and End User.

vendorId.description: Reference to Vendor. (Relationship: Vendor 1:N Conversation).  Required in all cases

endUserId.description: Reference to EndUser. (Relationship: EndUser 1:N Conversation). Nullable if conversation is between Super Admin and Vendor Admin.

startTime.description: Timestamp of when the conversation was started

Message.title: Message
Message.description: Represents a message within a conversation thread.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Message entity.

senderId.description: Reference to the user who sent the message. Could be SuperAdmin, VendorAdmin, or EndUser.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the message was sent.

FileStorage.title: FileStorage
FileStorage.description: Represents a file stored in Firebase Storage, with metadata.

id.description: Unique identifier for the file storage entry.

fileName.description: The original name of the file.

contentType.description: The MIME type of the file (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf').

fileSize.description: The size of the file in bytes.

uploadTimestamp.description: Timestamp of when the file was uploaded.

fileUrl.description: URL of the file stored in Firebase Storage.

vendorId.description: Reference to Vendor, if the file is related to a vendor. (Relationship: Vendor 1:N FileStorage)

endUserId.description: Reference to EndUser, if the file is related to an end user. (Relationship: EndUser 1:N FileStorage)

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure Authorization Independence, clarity, and scalability for the ParkX application.  Authorization Independence is achieved by denormalizing relevant authorization data (like vendorId) into subcollections where required. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules, enabling atomic operations.

**Structure Overview:**

*   `/super_admins/{superAdminId}`: Stores Super Admin profiles.
*   `/vendors/{vendorId}`: Stores Vendor profiles. Vendor documents also contain critical metadata like `superAdminId`.
*   `/users/{userId}`: Stores End User profiles. End Users are created at the top level and contain the vendorId of their associated vendor.
*   `/vendors/{vendorId}/parking_spots/{parkingSpotId}`: Stores Parking Spot data, segregated by vendor. The vendorId is denormalized to enable secure listing of parking spots based on vendor.
*   `/invoices/{invoiceId}`: Stores Invoice data. There is no parent/child relationship between Vendor/EndUser and Invoices. Invoices contain both `vendorId` and `endUserId`, either of which can be null.
*   `/conversations/{conversationId}`: Stores Conversation threads. The `vendorId` is stored on the document to avoid needing to look it up. Either `superAdminId` or `endUserId` may be set, but not both.
*   `/conversations/{conversationId}/messages/{messageId}`: Stores messages within a conversation. The `conversationId` field acts as the link. All messages for a given conversation share the same security profile.
*   `/file_storage/{fileStorageId}`: Stores metadata for files stored in Firebase Storage. Includes references to `vendorId` and `endUserId` for access control.
*   `/roles_super_admin/{userId}`: A presence-based role collection to efficiently check Super Admin status.

**Authorization Independence & Denormalization:**

*   Parking Spots: The `vendorId` is included within each `/vendors/{vendorId}/parking_spots/{parkingSpotId}` document. This allows security rules to validate that the vendor making changes to a parking spot is indeed the spot's owner, without needing to perform a `get()` on the parent Vendor document.
*   Messages: Messages are stored in a subcollection of conversations, and conversations contain either `superAdminId`, `vendorId`, or `endUserId` depending on who created the conversation. All messages for a given conversation share the same security requirements, and rules can be written to allow only participants of a conversation to post a message.
*   File Storage: Files are stored in the top-level collection `/file_storage/{fileStorageId}` and contain the `vendorId` or `endUserId` of the owner. This means the security rules can quickly determine the owner of a file, and whether or not the current user can access it.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

The structure facilitates secure list operations by segregating data based on ownership and role. For example, listing parking spots is always done within the context of a vendor (`/vendors/{vendorId}/parking_spots`).  The security rules can then ensure that only the specified vendor (or a Super Admin) can list those spots.  Similarly, the `roles_super_admin` collection uses existence checks, preventing the need to filter based on document content.

**Global Roles (DBAC):**

The `/roles_super_admin/{userId}` collection provides a simple and efficient way to check if a user has Super Admin privileges. The security rules only need to check for the existence of a document with the user's ID in this collection.
